title: Minimum Weighted Subgraph With the Required Paths II
summary: Given an undirected weighted tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a set of queries specifying source nodes, return an array where each element is the minimum weight of a subtree allowing travel from both source nodes to a destination node.
statement: Given an undirected weighted tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a set of queries specifying source nodes, return an array where each element is the minimum weight of a subtree allowing travel from both source nodes to a destination node.
constraints: edges form a weighted tree of up to 100,000 zero-indexed nodes.
Each query contains three pairwise distinct nodes: two sources and one destination.
Return the minimum total weight of a connected subtree containing all three query nodes.
hints: For three tree nodes, the union of their connecting paths counts every selected edge in exactly two of the three pairwise distances.
Preprocess root distances and binary-lifting ancestors, then answer each query with half the sum of its three pairwise distances.
Build parent jump levels; compute LCA-based distances for (a,b), (a,d), and (b,d); add and divide by two.
Unique tree paths make the required subtree their union, and every union edge separates one terminal from the other two, so it appears in exactly two pair distances.
editorial: Unique tree paths make the required subtree their union, and every union edge separates one terminal from the other two, so it appears in exactly two pair distances.

tests.explanation: The two required path unions weigh 12 and 11.
Both tree edges are necessary, so the subtree weighs 15.
